segments.t: Joining me now, Niccolo Damasi, the CEO of INQ.
Niccolo, it's always great to speak with you.
You're announcing an acquisition today.
You're doubling down on security.
Let's talk about it.
Yeah, well, look, INQ already is, I would argue,
the biggest quantum security company in the Western world.
We've been investing in this sector for over two years.
And I was, I believe, the first in the world
to say last June, 2025, that Q Day was coming a lot earlier
than everybody else thought.
So this is really an extension of that investment
into quantum key distribution, post-quantum cryptography,
and now we're adding zero trust and compartmentalization
to our defense in depth strategy.
This means that we can protect
not only critical infrastructure,
we believe better than anyone in the world,
but of course, the Fortune 500.
And so you and I have had these conversations
about Q Day coming faster than folks realize.
How much faster are we talking about,
and why does that mean
that you should be making this investment
and focusing on what I would say are the next chapters
beyond the ones that we're talking about day-to-day
on CNBC when it comes to cybersecurity?
Well, I said last June that Q Day was happening
probably by the end of this administration, the lab,
and then probably the following year out in the wild.
Pretty much everyone, I think, agrees with me now
a year, year and a half on.
The White House issued executive orders on June 22nd.
One of them was around securing the nation
for the quantum era.
The exciting thing about I&Q's technology,
including now that we have illicitly in the fold,
is that we're actually able to help people today
in the AI era,
in the GPU-based classical cybersecurity threat era.
Our technologies help you today.
They also set you up, of course,
as well as you can today for an era
where the bad guys will eventually get quantum computers.
They will eventually be able to marry them, I fear.
